title: Mouvement Républicain planned Stade Yougos rally denied by Brazzaville prefecture
reason: The March stadium meeting is documented as planned and prohibited; the available reports do not document its execution or attendance. It is therefore not coded as an actual gathering. The date is also inconsistent across sources (25 vs 26 March).
notes: The local CAD page says the party called for a March 25 meeting and the prefect barred it on March 23. CIVICUS describes a March 26 scheduled meeting and notes the March 25 date in the party’s renewed request; the Africa Center search snippet says the MR could not organize it. L’Horizon says a separate press conference followed the denial; that actual action is retained as E001 pending date/threshold/unit review. Do not confuse the planned stadium rally with E001.

title: Dolisie mobilization to form support committees for President Denis Sassou N’Guesso
reason: The report describes a support mobilization for the sitting President and launch of pro-President support committees. It does not document a protest demand directed to the Congolese state; social-benefit remarks are presented as the organizer’s program/promises, not as demands to government.
notes: The article says the campaign began in Brazzaville on February 23 and continued in Dolisie on March 9, with a Pointe-Noire event planned for the following month. No attendance count is given. This political-support series is not treated as a protest continuation or mass-action candidate.

title: Public-university professors’ strike and reported sit-ins in a ‘Congo’ (territory unresolved)
reason: The reprinted report does not identify the universities, event locations, or country. Its explicit MediaCongo attribution and Kinshasa-based page context do not establish that the activity occurred in the Republic of the Congo rather than the DRC, so it is not used as own-country evidence.
notes: The source mentions demonstrations and sit-ins but gives no participant count or event-specific dates. No connection to the February UMNG strike is inferred.
